usageNotes: Injects a raw keypress into a running VM's console via the QEMU monitor — useful for sending keys that the guest OS would otherwise intercept (e.g. Ctrl-Alt-Del, SysRq sequences) or for automating BIOS-level interactions. The VM must be in a running state on the specified node; sending to a stopped or paused VM will error. Key strings use QEMU monitor encoding (e.g. 'ctrl-alt-delete', 'ret', 'shift-f10').

examples.summary: Send Ctrl-Alt-Delete to a Windows VM to trigger a graceful restart

tips: Key names follow QEMU monitor conventions, not X11 or Windows virtual-key names — use 'ret' for Enter, 'spc' for Space, 'esc' for Escape.
To send a key chord, join key names with '-' (e.g. 'ctrl-alt-delete'). For individual keys in sequence, make separate API calls.
Only root (PAM) may use skiplock=true; API tokens for regular users cannot bypass locks even with VM.Console.
This returns null synchronously — there is no UPID or task to poll; the keypress is delivered immediately or the call fails.
